metadata.title: Yang-Mills Existence, Mass Gap and Nontriviality for Fixed Compact Simple Gauge Groups via Karcher Blocking and Exact Haar-Pivot Matching
metadata.description:
For four-dimensional pure Yang–Mills theory with any fixed compact connected simple gauge group G, this paper constructs a directed zero-spacing, infinite-volume limit of reflection-positive Wilson lattice measures. For the local gauge-invariant curvature-jet observable theory, the limiting Schwinger family is tempered, permutation symmetric, reflection positive, translation continuous, exponentially clustering, and O(4) covariant. Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction yields a positive-energy Poincaré-covariant local theory with a unique vacuum, a strictly positive Hamiltonian gap, and nontrivial local spectral content.

The construction is organized in four stages:

Ultraviolet construction and universal coefficient (§§2–5). A weighted forty-nine-path Karcher block—one straight path and forty-eight signed-corner staples—is placed in a complete sixteen-alias normal chart with a uniformly contractive, exponentially local right inverse. The linear block certificate is independent of color and tensors with the identity on Lie(G); the nonlinear constants are verified for each fixed group. A representation-normalized charged large-field partition, permanent rooted analytic domain, summed replica–BKAR logarithm, Wick-stable jet block, and centered invariant graph produce a uniform scale-two renormalization map. On the centered weak trajectory,

u(2L) = u(L) + (11 C₂(G) log 2)/(24π²) · u(L)² + O(u(L)³)

where C₂(G) is the adjoint Casimir. The quadratic coefficient is identified through an exact measure-level, unit-tangent analytic conjugacy between the Karcher invariant-graph coordinate and the standard renormalized background coupling, with the complete lattice BPHZL and Reisz hypotheses verified at fixed nonexceptional external momentum.

Directed physical-scale handoff (§6). A directed joint cutoff-and-volume schedule follows the weak trajectory to a controlled first-crossing class. Exact backward shooting fixes the physical scale, and a cofinal choice of terminal volume sends the lattice spacing to zero and the physical periodic volume to infinity. Carrier-adapted product coordinates separate retained holonomies from live fine-detail pivots while preserving the complete conditional measure; the compact-group landing uses a fixed-group Sobolev order exceeding dim G/4.

Exact Haar–optical matching and boundary-to-center closure (§§6–8). The compact Haar variables and optical normal fields remain in one exact partition function. All one-pivot contributions are absorbed into normalized conditional reference measures, while genuine multipivot interactions enter a convergent polymer expansion. A single marked replica–BKAR forest forces every boundary-to-center path to pay separated Haar contraction, optical covariance decay, or pre-existing support charge, producing one uniform physical exponential-clustering rate.

Continuum reconstruction, mass gap, and nontriviality (§§9–11). A least-label multiscale source forest transports local gauge-invariant curvature jets through the ultraviolet corridor and compact matching regime. Displacement, stress, contact, and rotation-defect Ward identities, complete dimension-four mixing, and a dimension-six rotation regulator establish the limiting O(4)-covariant Schwinger hierarchy. Reflection-positive recombination and Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction give the unique vacuum and strictly positive gap m★(G). Endpoint-safe curvature-source transport produces a nonzero reflected local vector with positive spectral mass in a finite interval [m★(G), M★(G)] above the gap.

External-input boundary (§1). Every imported theorem is isolated in an explicit standard-input register: the BKAR forest formula, the Kotecký–Preiss polymer theorem, Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction, the Lüscher–Weisz background-field identities, lattice BPHZ/BPHZL and Reisz power counting, and the universal one-loop Yang–Mills coefficient. All model-specific estimates are developed within the manuscript. The appendices supply the endpoint packet-shell verification, root-data normalizations, the specialization map to the SU(2) companion, and representative certifications for SU(4), Sp(2), and G₂.

Scope and generality (§12). The theorem concerns the local gauge-invariant curvature-jet observable sector for each fixed compact connected simple gauge group. It does not claim group-uniform estimates, a simultaneous large-rank limit, control of every extended Wilson-line or generalized-symmetry sector, or uniqueness of the continuum limit outside the directed construction.
metadata.notes:
Major-version release. Version 4.0 replaces the rank-one scope of Version 3.0 with a self-contained theorem for arbitrary fixed compact connected simple GGG. It adds representation-normalized charged complements, fixed-group Karcher and toron admission, dimension-adapted Peter–Weyl landing, ordered noncommuting multijets, general invariant-jet spaces, and the coefficient 11CA(G)log⁡2/(24π2). Version 3.0 remains the complete SU(2) specialization.

Version 3.0 remains remains the complete SU(2) specialization and is permanently available and separately citable at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21479499. The present manuscript is self-contained and does not use the SU(2) theorem as a logical input. It establishes the corresponding construction for every fixed compact connected simple Lie group G, together with a fixed faithful finite-dimensional unitary representation. All constants may depend on G and on the chosen representation.
